subject.title: Feature: durable natural-language rule learning + explicit multi-mention reply semantics

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class durable conversational rule-governance layer and cross-channel explicit multi-bot mention semantics, or keep this work split across memory/plugin APIs and channel-specific fixes?
rationale: The remaining work changes memory authority, persisted rule storage, workspace-file precedence, conflict handling, and channel reply semantics, and current source shows adjacent mechanisms but no existing contract that makes this a strict bug fix.

options.title: Keep As Design Tracker
options.body: Define rule authority, storage, promotion review, conflict precedence, and channel mention semantics before implementation proceeds.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Trackers
options.body: Use the Feishu issues and PRs for message-loss delivery fixes, and open a separate memory-governance design only if maintainers want durable conversational rules.

options.title: Route Through Plugin API First
options.body: Require a plugin or memory API design to prove the capability cannot be built outside core before adding a core rule layer.

recommendation.title: Keep As Design Tracker
recommendation.body: Define rule authority, storage, promotion review, conflict precedence, and channel mention semantics before implementation proceeds.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans prompt/context authority, memory promotion, plugin boundaries, and Feishu/group delivery semantics where Peter Steinberger has the strongest sampled cross-surface history.
